summary: On July 22, 2026 an attacker used compromised private keys for five of the seven validators of the AFX Trade bridge, which serves the Arbitrum-based decentralized perpetuals exchange, to pass the bridge's signature threshold and withdraw about $24.15 million in USDC, which was bridged to Ethereum and swapped for ETH. The bridge contract itself was not flawed; it accepted valid signatures. AFX offered the attacker a 30% bounty to return the rest, and analysts later linked the theft to North Korean hackers through shared laundering addresses.
